description: QUANTUSSY CELL — one cell of a Quantussy ring after Peter Blasser and Richard Brewster: an LFO whose rate is sampled and held from a neighbouring cell, giving slow chaotic voltages.

params.text: Sets the resting rate of the oscillator, an eighth of a hertz up to 8Hz.
Scales the sampled CV before it shifts the rate, from full inversion through silence to full.
Sets the floor the rate is held above, from a thousandth of a hertz up to 1kHz.
Sets the ceiling the rate is held below, from a thousandth of a hertz up to 1kHz.

inputs.text: The voltage here is sampled on each rising edge of this cell's square wave and passed on unchanged; in a ring it is fed from a wave output of another cell.
The voltage here is sampled on each rising edge of this cell's square wave and shifts the rate; in a ring it is fed from the castle output of another cell.
Adds to the scaling of the sampled CV, 10% per volt.
Raises the floor the rate is held above by one octave per volt.
Raises the ceiling the rate is held below by one octave per volt.

outputs.text: Carries the voltage sampled at the castle input, held until the next rising edge of this cell's square wave; in a ring it feeds the CV input of the next cell.
The sine of the oscillator, plus or minus 5V.
The triangle of the oscillator, plus or minus 5V.
The sawtooth of the oscillator, plus or minus 5V.
The square of the oscillator, plus or minus 5V; its rising edges are what clock the two sample and holds in this cell.

notes: one cell on its own is a plain LFO; the chaos comes from a ring of cells, five or seven of them.
to build the ring, patch each cell's castle output to the next cell's CV input and one of its wave outputs to that next cell's castle input, then close the ring back to the first cell.

inputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.4: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
